name: Insight Memo
tagline: Turn analysis into a memo people act on
about: Insight Memo turns your findings into a one-page memo, a readout deck outline and plain-English number comparisons, and rehearses the questions stakeholders will fire back.
persona: You are a data-storytelling coach: bottom line up front, one message per section, every number given a comparison, and honest about uncertainty.

onboarding.title: From findings to decisions
onboarding.subtitle: Who reads your work? That shapes the tone.

tools.title: Write the memo
tools.subtitle: Findings → one page

inputs.label: Your findings (rough notes are fine)
inputs.placeholder: churn up 0.5pt since price rise, mostly monthly plans, annual unaffected, billing tickets doubled

inputs.label: Decision or ask
inputs.placeholder: approve grandfathering monthly customers for 3 months

tools.prompt: Write a one-page insight memo from {findings} with the ask '{ask}' for the profile's readers and tone. Text with a 2-sentence bottom line, bullets 'What we found' (each with the number and its comparison), a table 'Options' (Option | Expected effect | Cost | Risk), kv (recommendation, confidence, what would change our mind, next check-in), and a callout on data limitations.

tools.title: Readout deck outline
tools.subtitle: Slide by slide

inputs.label: What you analysed and found
inputs.placeholder: analysed 6 months of support tickets: 40% are password resets, peak Monday mornings

tools.prompt: Outline a {slides}-slide readout for: {analysis}. Table 'Slides' (# | Headline as a full-sentence takeaway | Visual | Speaker note), steps for the opening 60 seconds, a quote with the closing slide's recommendation text, and a callout on what belongs in the appendix.

tools.title: Make numbers land
tools.subtitle: Comparisons people remember
tools.prompt: Rewrite {numbers} so non-analysts feel them. Table 'Translations' (Number | Plain-English version | Comparison or analogy | When to use it), bullets of rounding and framing rules, and a callout on comparisons that mislead (per cent vs percentage points, relative vs absolute, small bases).

tools.title: Stakeholder questions
tools.subtitle: What they'll ask and how to answer

inputs.label: Your main claim and evidence
inputs.placeholder: recommend pausing paid social: CAC doubled in Q2 with no lift in retention

tools.prompt: For the claim '{summary}', list the 8 hardest questions the profile's readers will ask as a table (Question | Why they ask it | Best answer | Evidence to have ready), a checklist of analyses to run beforehand, and a quote with a graceful answer for a question you cannot answer yet.

tools.title: Chart caption & takeaway
tools.subtitle: One chart, one sentence

inputs.label: Or describe the chart
inputs.placeholder: weekly active users by platform, iOS flat, Android +30%

tools.prompt: Write the takeaway for the chart in the photo or described as: {chart}. Quote with 3 takeaway titles, kv (caption, source line, footnote on caveats), and bullets on what a reader might misread.
